headline: Only 8 of 45 super funds meet the retirement support benchmark; most members arrive at retirement with no simple advice pathway and are offered expensive comprehensive advice at $4,000–$5,000 or a generic default transfer to an account-based pension
reasoning: Chant West designed a 20-criteria assessment covering products (account-based pensions, lifetime income products, retirement bonuses), advice and guidance (financial calculators, seminars, nudges), and service quality (call-centre responsiveness, payment turnaround). This year's pass mark was raised to 14 out of 20 criteria. Only eight funds passed: Australian Retirement Trust, Aware Super, Brighter Super, Host Plus, Uni Super (returning), plus new entrants AMP, Colonial First State, and Vision Super. The broader problem is that most funds funnel retiring members into a default account-based pension with no tailored guidance, while comprehensive advice costs $4,000–$5,000 and deters most members. Chant West provides individual fund report cards to direct improvement.
quote: Too often, when someone gets to retirement, they're told, okay, I've got to say, let's say half $1 million, I've got a half $1 million in the super. And I got on the phone and say, I've just retired. What do I do? And the fund says he can transfer this from super into pension. And that's where you can draw your money out from and that's good. But then someone says, okay, I'll transfer it across, but what do I do with it there? How much should I be taking out? How should I have it invested, etc.? So there's lots of choices that need to be made. And in the majority of funds, what happens is they're generally told, okay, we can give you comprehensive advice, but that might cost 4 or $5000. And a lot of people don't want to pay that. And they're not complicated enough to really have to spend that money. So what we're really wanting is funds to provide some simple financial advice at that point, to move them from where they are at the moment in super to where they should be in an account based pension or another pension product that's going to work for them.
episode_title: Super funds fall short on retirement support | the advisory

headline: Most super funds are failing members in the retirement (decumulation) phase — only 8 funds earn the Epic Retirement tick across 20 criteria, and the industry must shift focus from accumulation to drawdown usability
reasoning: Ian Fryer notes that the superannuation industry has historically focused on the accumulation phase but needs to urgently pivot to supporting members through retirement drawdown, given approximately 2.5 million Australians are forecast to retire over the next decade. Chant West assesses funds against 20 criteria under the Epic Retirement framework, and only eight funds currently achieve the overall Epic tick. Funds that fall short receive a private report card detailing what they do and do not provide, directing them toward what members actually need. Fryer highlights operational shortcomings such as payment settlement times — most super funds take a day or more to transfer money, versus instant Osko payments via banks — as examples of friction that makes it hard for members to use their savings effectively. The core message is that super funds need to make it easy for members to make the right decisions and then act on them quickly.
quote: The whole point of the super is not the saving up. It's actually the taking out. And we need to and funds need to be run in a way that makes it easier to take money up. Like, for example, if I was to pay, um, someone some money. I'd generally be through my bank and, um, I would pay using Osco payments where it goes immediately to the other party. That's not how most super funds work. It might take a day or so for the money to go across. So we're looking for things like that which just make it more possible for members to say, okay, superannuation. That's my pot of money. I can use that as I need to, um, I can use that. And it's easy to use too often. Super funds make it too hard for members to do stuff.
episode_title: Super funds fall short on retirement support | the advisory
